subject: Re: Finex - Post-call: Performance & Throughput sizing (latency SLOs)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Cc: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Finex — Post-call recap & next steps (performance / throughput)

Sarah — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can size correctly and put together a Dedicated / test plan: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: real-time transaction enrichment used in customer dashboards and alerts.
- Latency SLO target: p50 ~50–100ms, p95 250–350ms (you said p95 goal is ~300ms).
- Traffic shape: steady-state ~20k tokens/sec (aggregate across requests); peak bursts up to ~100k tokens/sec during daily batch and market-open spikes.
- Concurrency: ~150–250 concurrent active users; peak spikes driven by batch replay jobs and streaming websocket fans.
- Request sizes: average payload ~512 tokens, max ~2048 tokens.
- Streaming: yes — partial tokens need to be streamed to the client for progressive updates.

Open items / ask from Finex (please confirm):
1) Confirm p95 SLO target you want Redwood to size for (you mentioned 300ms).
2) Clarify steady vs peak windows and expected duration of peaks (minutes/hours).
3) Share a representative sample of request payloads (or redacted logs) and one hour of QPS timeline if available.
4) Permission to run a short, synthetic load test in your staging environment (we'll coordinate schedule).

What we'll deliver after confirmation:
- A throughput sizing worksheet (attached) with tokens/sec, QPS, and estimated Dedicated cluster configuration.
- Latency projections (p50/p95) across the proposed config and a recommended canary test plan.
- Suggested batching/kv-cache settings and quantization profiles to reduce unit cost while meeting SLOs.

Next steps:
- Sarah to confirm items (1)-(3) above and upload the metrics export (CSV).
- We will return a preliminary sizing within 48 hours of receiving the sample payloads.

Thanks — Rafael

Thanks Rafael — great summary. A few clarifications and I've attached the one-hour export you requested (finex-metrics-export.csv):

- Confirmed SLO: p95 300ms (we can relax to 350ms for bulk-batch replays but real-time dashboards need 300ms).
- Steady-state: weekdays 24/7 at ~20k tokens/sec.
- Peak: 11:50–12:10 and 16:00–16:20 local time, spikes up to ~100k tokens/sec lasting ~10–20 minutes.
- Concurrency: average active sessions ~180; peak concurrent connections ~230.
- Payloads: avg tokens/request ~520; 95th percentile ~1300; max 2048.
- Streaming: required for the dashboard — clients start rendering after first chunks. We need per-token-ish streaming with low inter-chunk latency.
- Traffic profile: ~70% interactive dashboard traffic, ~20% scheduled batch replays, ~10% async backfill.

I gave you the CSV with timestamps and token counts for the hour we discussed. Also attached a small sample of redacted request payloads in the drive link I shared (see HubSpot note).

You have permission to run a synthetic load test in our staging cluster Wednesday 08/11 between 10:00–14:00 PDT. We'll provision a test CI token and a dedicated staging subdomain — I'll send the access details in a separate email.

Sarah

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Finex — Post-call recap & next steps (performance / throughput)

Sarah — thanks for the data and the staging window. Attached is our preliminary throughput estimate (finex-throughput-estimate.xlsx) — high level notes below: 

Prelim sizing highlights (high level):
- Steady-state (20k tokens/sec): roughly corresponds to ~38 requests/sec given avg 520 tokens/request. We project p95 ~220–280ms on a small Dedicated pool with default batching and prefix caching enabled.
- Peak burst (100k tokens/sec for 10–20 minutes): ~190 requests/sec. To maintain p95<=300ms during the burst we recommend a dedicated burst pool (hot autoscale policy) sized to handle the 100k tokens/sec window; this is a ~4–5x uplift from the steady config.
- Streaming: recommend enabling streaming-optimized kernels + shorter batch windows (5–10ms target) for the dashboard path; will increase CPU/GPU overhead but keeps inter-chunk latency under 40ms in our tests.
- QPS vs tokens/sec mapping and cost table included in the spreadsheet.

Next steps (for the test on 08/11):
1) Sarah to provide staging access details and the CI token.
2) We'll share a short test plan (canary -> ramp -> soak) and our synthetic payload generator.
3) Run two passes: steady-state 60m run and two 15-min burst runs that mimic your 11:50–12:10 pattern.

If that sounds good I'll schedule time with our infra team to provision the Dedicated test cluster and confirm timelines.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
